questions.subject: costing
questions.stem: Under marginal costing, fixed production overhead incurred during a period is:

options.text: Included in the cost of closing inventory on normal capacity
options.error: absorption-costing treatment
options.label: A

options.text: Charged in full to the profit and loss account of that period
options.label: B

options.text: Apportioned to units produced on actual capacity
options.error: absorption on actual basis
options.label: C

options.text: Carried forward and charged when the goods are sold
options.error: confuses deferral with product cost
options.label: D

steps: Marginal costing treats only variable costs as product costs.
Fixed production overhead is a period cost: written off in full against contribution of the period.
Inventory is therefore valued at variable (marginal) cost only.
explanation.formula_used: Profit = Contribution − Fixed cost
explanation.trap: Absorption costing is the one that carries fixed overhead into inventory.

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

questions.microtopic_name: Absorption vs marginal costing — profit reconciliation

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem: A product sells at ₹80 per unit with a variable cost of ₹52 per unit. Its P/V ratio is:

options.error: absolute contribution ₹28 read as a percentage
options.label: A

options.error: contribution divided by variable cost
options.label: C

options.error: variable cost ratio taken as P/V
options.label: D

explanation.formula_used: P/V ratio = Contribution ÷ Sales
explanation.trap: Divide by selling price, never by variable cost.

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

questions.microtopic_name: Marginal costing — contribution and P/V ratio

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem: Fixed costs are ₹4,20,000, selling price ₹150 and variable cost ₹90 per unit. Break-even point in units is:

options.error: divided by (SP + VC) instead of (SP − VC)
options.label: A

options.error: fixed cost divided by variable cost
options.label: B

options.error: fixed cost divided by selling price
options.label: C

explanation.formula_used: BEP (units) = Fixed cost ÷ Contribution per unit
explanation.trap: Denominator is contribution, not price.

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

questions.microtopic_name: Break-even point in units and value

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem: Actual sales are 50,000 units and break-even sales are 35,000 units. The margin of safety ratio is:

options.error: divided by (actual + BEP)
options.label: A

options.error: margin of safety divided by BEP instead of actual sales
options.label: B

options.error: BEP as a share of sales, not the excess
options.label: C

explanation.formula_used: MOS ratio = (Actual sales − BEP sales) ÷ Actual sales
explanation.trap: The base is actual sales.

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

questions.microtopic_name: Margin of safety and angle of incidence

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem:
A firm reports:

| Period | Sales (₹) | Profit (₹) |
|---|---:|---:|
| I | 2,00,000 | 20,000 |
| II | 2,60,000 | 38,000 |

Assuming no change in selling price, variable cost ratio or fixed cost, the fixed cost is:

options.error: Period I contribution reported as fixed cost
options.label: A

options.error: change in profit reported as fixed cost
options.label: B

options.error: profit added to contribution instead of subtracted
options.label: C

steps: P/V = change in profit ÷ change in sales = 18,000 ÷ 60,000 = 30%
explanation.formula_used: P/V = ΔProfit ÷ ΔSales; FC = Contribution − Profit
explanation.trap: Profit is subtracted from contribution to get fixed cost.

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

questions.microtopic_name: Marginal costing — contribution and P/V ratio

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem: Fixed costs are ₹3,60,000 and the P/V ratio is 40%. Sales required to earn a profit of ₹1,20,000 are:

options.error: break-even sales; target profit ignored
options.label: A

options.error: divided by variable cost ratio
options.label: B

options.error: profit added to BEP sales without grossing up
options.label: C

explanation.formula_used: Required sales = (FC + Target profit) ÷ P/V
explanation.trap: Target profit must be grossed up by the P/V ratio too.

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

questions.microtopic_name: Target-profit sales

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem: No opening stock. Production 12,000 units, sales 10,000 units. Fixed production overhead ₹2,40,000, absorbed on actual production. Compared with marginal costing, profit under absorption costing is:

options.error: overhead rate computed on units sold
options.label: A

options.error: direction reversed
options.label: B

options.error: ignores fixed overhead carried in closing stock
options.label: C

steps: Closing stock = 2,000 units carries 2,000 × 20 = 40,000 of fixed overhead
That amount is deferred under absorption costing, so absorption profit is higher by it.
explanation.formula_used: Profit difference = Fixed OH in closing stock − Fixed OH in opening stock
explanation.trap: When production exceeds sales, absorption profit is higher.

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

questions.microtopic_name: Absorption vs marginal costing — profit reconciliation

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem: Sales are ₹10,00,000, profit ₹90,000 and the P/V ratio 30%. The margin of safety ratio is:

options.error: profit multiplied by P/V instead of divided
options.label: A

options.error: BEP ratio reported instead of MOS
options.label: B

options.error: profit-to-sales ratio taken as MOS
options.label: D

explanation.formula_used: Profit = MOS × P/V
explanation.trap: MOS ratio × P/V ratio = Profit ÷ Sales.

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

questions.microtopic_name: Margin of safety and angle of incidence

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem: Selling price ₹100, variable cost ₹60 per unit, fixed cost ₹4,00,000, current sales 15,000 units. If price is cut by 10%, units needed to keep the present profit are:

options.error: new break-even point; present profit ignored
options.label: A

options.error: variable cost also cut by 10%
options.label: C

options.error: volume raised by the same 10% as the price cut
options.label: D

explanation.formula_used: Units = (FC + Target profit) ÷ New contribution per unit
explanation.trap: A 10% price cut lowered unit contribution by 25% here, so volume must rise by a third.

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

questions.microtopic_name: Target-profit sales

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem:
Machine hours are the limiting factor.

| Product | Contribution per unit (₹) | Machine hours per unit |
|---|---:|---:|
| A | 60 | 4 |
| B | 45 | 2 |
| C | 80 | 5 |

The order of priority for production is:

options.error: ranked by contribution per unit
options.label: B

options.error: ranked by fewest hours per unit
options.label: C

options.error: ranking reversed
options.label: D

steps: Contribution per hour: A = 60/4 = ₹15; B = 45/2 = ₹22.5; C = 80/5 = ₹16
Rank highest first: B, C, A
explanation.formula_used: Rank by contribution per unit of the key factor
explanation.trap: Contribution per unit is irrelevant once a resource binds.

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

questions.microtopic_name: Key factor and product mix decisions

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem:
Available machine hours are 20,000; fixed cost ₹1,50,000.

| Product | Contribution/unit (₹) | Hours/unit | Max demand (units) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 60 | 4 | 5,000 |
| B | 45 | 2 | 3,000 |
| C | 80 | 5 | 2,000 |

Maximum profit is:

options.error: total contribution reported; fixed cost not deducted
options.label: A

options.error: mix ranked by contribution per unit
options.label: B

options.error: demand ceiling ignored for the top-ranked product
options.label: D

steps: Rank by contribution per hour: B, C, A
explanation.formula_used: Allocate the key factor in rank order, capped by demand
explanation.trap: Respect demand limits before moving down the ranking.

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

questions.microtopic_name: Key factor and product mix decisions

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem: Capacity 50,000 units; current sales 40,000 units at ₹50; variable cost ₹30 per unit. A one-time order for 12,000 units at ₹38 would require an extra ₹20,000 of fixed cost and, due to capacity, the loss of some regular sales. Net effect on profit of accepting is:

options.error: displaced sales and extra fixed cost ignored
options.label: A

options.error: displaced regular sales ignored
options.label: B

options.error: extra fixed cost ignored
options.label: D

explanation.formula_used: Net gain = Order contribution − Displaced contribution − Incremental fixed cost
explanation.trap: Spare capacity is only 10,000 units; the last 2,000 units displace full-price sales.

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

questions.microtopic_name: Sunk, differential, opportunity and relevant costs

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem:
Two products are sold in the ratio 3 : 2 by units.

| | X | Y |
|---|---:|---:|
| Selling price (₹) | 40 | 75 |
| Variable cost (₹) | 24 | 57 |

Fixed cost is ₹3,78,000. Break-even sales value is:

options.error: 3 : 2 applied as a value mix, not a unit mix
options.label: B

options.error: simple average of the two P/V ratios
options.label: C

options.error: P/V of product Y alone
options.label: D

explanation.formula_used: Composite BEP = FC ÷ Weighted contribution per mix
explanation.trap: Weights must follow the stated mix basis (units here).

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

questions.microtopic_name: Break-even point in units and value

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem: Plan A: fixed cost ₹2,00,000, variable cost 60% of sales. Plan B: fixed cost ₹3,20,000, variable cost 45% of sales. Plan B gives the higher profit above sales of:

options.error: break-even of Plan B
options.label: A

options.error: break-even of Plan A
options.label: C

options.error: divided by Plan B's variable ratio instead of the difference
options.label: D

steps: Above this point the lower variable-cost plan (B) earns more.
explanation.formula_used: Indifference point = ΔFixed cost ÷ ΔVariable cost ratio
explanation.trap: Not a break-even point; it compares two structures.

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

questions.microtopic_name: Break-even point in units and value

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem: Fixed cost is ₹6,00,000. If operations are suspended, ₹2,40,000 of it is avoidable, but closing and reopening costs ₹60,000. Contribution is ₹20 per unit. The shut-down point is:

options.error: break-even point
options.label: B

options.error: cost if shut ÷ contribution
options.label: C

options.error: shut-down cost ignored
options.label: D

steps: Operating is worthwhile while fixed cost − contribution < 4,20,000
explanation.formula_used: Shut-down point = (Total FC − Cost if shut) ÷ Contribution per unit
explanation.trap: Below this volume, closing loses less than operating.

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

questions.microtopic_name: Make-or-buy and shutdown decisions

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem: Opening stock 2,000 units carried fixed overhead at ₹18 per unit. This period: production 10,000 units, fixed production overhead ₹2,00,000 absorbed on actual output, sales 11,000 units (FIFO). Compared with absorption costing, marginal costing profit is:

options.error: closing stock overhead ignored
options.label: B

options.error: opening stock revalued at the current rate
options.label: C

options.error: direction reversed
options.label: D

steps: Absorption − Marginal = 20,000 − 36,000 = −16,000, so marginal is higher
explanation.formula_used: Difference = Fixed OH in closing stock − Fixed OH in opening stock
explanation.trap: Opening stock keeps its own (prior) rate.

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

questions.microtopic_name: Absorption vs marginal costing — profit reconciliation

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem:
**Case — Vardhan Home Appliances Ltd (fictional)**

Annual data:

| | Mixer | Iron | Kettle |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Units sold | 20,000 | 30,000 | 25,000 |
| Selling price per unit (₹) | 1,200 | 800 | 600 |
| Variable cost per unit (₹) | 780 | 600 | 540 |

Total fixed cost of ₹1,26,00,000 is apportioned to products in proportion to sales value. On this basis the Kettle shows a loss.

If the Kettle is discontinued, only ₹9,00,000 of its apportioned fixed cost is saved (specific supervision). Company profit after discontinuing will be:

options.error: specific fixed cost saving ignored
options.label: A

options.error: saving added but Kettle contribution not given up
options.label: C

options.error: apportioned 'loss' of Kettle simply removed
options.label: D

steps: Present profit = total contribution 1,59,00,000 − fixed cost 1,26,00,000 = 33,00,000
Kettle contribution lost = 15,00,000; specific cost saved = 9,00,000
explanation.formula_used: Decision = Contribution forgone vs avoidable fixed cost
explanation.trap: Apportioned fixed cost is not saved by dropping a product.

source_refs.note: Standard marginal costing/CVP pattern (ICAI/ICMAI cost accounting syllabus). Original figures and entities; no text reproduced.

Total fixed cost of ₹1,26,00,000 is apportioned to products in proportion to sales value. On this basis the Kettle shows a loss.

At the present sales mix, the company's break-even sales value is:

Annual data:

Total fixed cost of ₹1,26,00,000 is apportioned to products in proportion to sales value. On this basis the Kettle shows a loss.

The margin of safety ratio at the present sales mix is:

options.error: BEP ratio reported instead of MOS

options.error: BEP taken from Iron's P/V

questions.microtopic_name: Margin of safety and angle of incidence

questions.subject: costing
questions.stem:
**Case — Vardhan Home Appliances Ltd (fictional)**

Annual data:

| | Mixer | Iron | Kettle |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Units sold | 20,000 | 30,000 | 25,000 |
| Selling price per unit (₹) | 1,200 | 800 | 600 |
| Variable cost per unit (₹) | 780 | 600 | 540 |

Total fixed cost of ₹1,26,00,000 is apportioned to products in proportion to sales value. On this basis the Kettle shows a loss.

Management proposes replacing the Kettle with a Toaster on the same capacity: 20,000 units at ₹700, variable cost ₹520, and new specific fixed cost of ₹12,00,000. The Kettle's specific cost of ₹9,00,000 would be saved. The change in company profit is:

options.error: Kettle's specific cost saving ignored
options.label: A

options.error: both specific fixed costs ignored
options.label: B

options.error: Kettle contribution forgone ignored
options.label: D

steps: Kettle given up: contribution 15,00,000 − specific cost 9,00,000 = 6,00,000
explanation.formula_used: Incremental profit = New net contribution − Net contribution given up
explanation.trap: Compare specific (avoidable) figures on both sides; ignore apportioned cost.
